newsitem.title: UK: Barclays ups profit in H1, buy-back bigger.
newsitem.headline: Barclays ups profit in H1, buy-back bigger.

text.p: British bank Barclays Plc on Thursday reported pre-tax profits up eight percent to 1.376 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) and also said it would have greater than expected scope for share buy-backs this year.

Barclays raised its dividend by 17 percent to 13.5 pence per share. After adjustments for measures in July's UK budget, Barclays pre-tax figure was virtually flat at 1.27 billion pounds but underlying operating profit gained 11 percent to 1.33 billion.

Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor said in the results statement the present combination of strong economic growth and low inflation provided a favourable climate. He said the group was using this to focus on the quality and sustainability of earnings should a more challenging business environment come about.
This critically meant not being fooled into compromising risk standards, he said.
Barclays said every major business in the group was meeting or exceeding expectations and return on equity remained high at 24 percent.
Barclays shares were expected to open higher as traders greeted the results and buy-back news.

Its investment banking arm BZW had made an operating profit of 124 million pounds ($198.6 million) in the first half, down from 148 million a year earlier, and also revealed a 20 million pounds loss in equity derivatives associated with the British budget in May, in which the dividend tax regime was changed.

Barclays said BZW's operating profit "recovered substantially from the second half of 1996 although, because of the continued planned investment in people and technology in 1997, it is below the result achieved in the first half of the year".
A threat of an overtime ban hangs over the bank's retail operations in Britain but the company expects the impact to be minimal. ($ = 0.624 British Pounds)
